paper.title: Double Thompson Sampling for Dueling Bandits

unmapped: Copeland winner objective: regret measured via normalized Copeland scores zeta_i of the two chosen arms, R(T) = zeta* T - 1/2 sum_t E[zeta_{a1} + zeta_{a2}]
Stationary preference matrix P with p_ij + p_ji = 1, p_ii = 1/2; comparison outcomes are Bernoulli(p_ij)
Condorcet dueling bandits included as special case zeta* = 1
settings.definition_quote: The performance of a dueling bandit algorithm $\Gamma$ is measured by its expected cumulative regret, which is defined as R_{\Gamma}(T) = \zeta^* T - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{t = 1}^T \mathbb{E} [ \zeta_{a_t^{(1)}} + \zeta_{a_t^{(2)}}].

symbols.sum_pairs_lose: sum over ordered pairs (i,j), i != j, with p_ij < 1/2
symbols.alpha_rucb: RUCB/RLCB scale parameter alpha of D-TS

conditions: Assumption 1: p_ij != 1/2 for all i != j

source.label: thm:regret_copeland
source.quote: When applying D-TS with $\alpha > 0.5$ in a Copeland dueling bandit with a preference matrix $P = [p_{ij}]_{K \times K}$ satisfying Assumption~1, its regret is bounded as: R_{D-TS}(T) \leq \sum_{i\neq j: p_{ij} < 1/2}\bigg[\frac{4\alpha\log T}{\Delta_{ij}^2} + (1+ \epsilon) \frac{\log T}{D(p_{ij}||1/2)}\bigg] +O(\frac{K^2}{\epsilon^2}), where $\epsilon > 0$ is an arbitrary constant

results.notes: Leading terms are explicit; only the additive K^2/eps^2 term is in O(). Overall O(K^2 log T). Regret defined via Copeland scores in expectation -> pseudo_regret; comparator is the Copeland winner. Algorithm uses log t so anytime.

bound.expression: W_terms*log(T) + U_terms*4*alpha_rucb*log(T) + beta_alg*(1 + eps_alg)**2*V_terms*log(log(T)) + K**3 + K**2/eps_alg**2

symbols.W_terms: sum over Copeland winners i of [sum_{j: p_ji>1/2} 4 alpha/Delta_ji^2 + sum_{j: p_ji<1/2} (1+eps)/D(p_ji||1/2)]
symbols.U_terms: sum over non-winners i of sum_{j=1}^{L_C+1} 1/Delta_{sigma_i(j),i}^2
symbols.V_terms: sum over non-winners i of sum_{j=L_C+2}^K 1/D(p_{sigma_i(j),i} || p_{sigma_i(L_C+1),i})
symbols.L_C: number of arms that beat a Copeland winner

conditions: Assumption 1: p_ij != 1/2 for all i != j
Assumption 2: for each non-winner i, p_{sigma_i(L_C+1),i} > p_{sigma_i(j),i} for all j > L_C+1 (no ties)

source.label: thm:regret_dts_plus
source.quote: The regret of D-TS$^+$, $R_{\dtsp}(T)$, satisfies inequality \eqref{eq:regret_copeland_refined} under Assumptions~1 and 2.

results.notes: Same bound as Theorem 1 transferred to D-TS+ (only tie-breaking differs).

source.label: thm:cmp_bounds_less_0p5
source.quote: Under D-TS, for an arbitrary constant $\epsilon>0$ and one pair $(i,j)$ with $p_{ji}<1/2$, we have \mathbb{E}[N^{(1)}_{ij}(T)] \leq (1+ \epsilon) \frac{\log T}{D(p_{ji}||1/2)} + O(\frac{1}{\epsilon^2}).

results.notes: Bound on expected number of comparisons (a1,a2)=(i,j).

source.label: thm:cmp_bounds_larger_0p5
source.quote: Under D-TS with $\alpha > 0.5$, for one pair $(i, j)$ with $p_{ji} >1/2$, we have \mathbb{E}[N^{(1)}_{ij}(T)] \leq \frac{4 \alpha \log T}{\Delta_{ji}^2} + O(1).

conditions: arm i not a Copeland winner

source.label: thm:cmp_bounds_eq_0p5
source.quote: Under D-TS, for any arm $i \notin \mathcal{C}^*$, we have \mathbb{E}[N_{ii}(T)] \leq O(K) + \sum_{k: p_{ki} > 1/2} \Theta\big( \frac{1}{\Delta_{ki}^2} + \frac{1}{\Delta_{ki}^2 D(1/2|| p_{ki})} + \frac{1}{\Delta_{ki}^4}\big) = O(K).

results.notes: Bound on self-comparisons of a non-winner arm; O(K) hides instance-dependent constants in Delta_ki.

conditions: arm i not a Copeland winner and j > L_C + 1

source.label: thm:regret_refined_singlearm
source.quote: Under Assumptions~1 and 2, for any suboptimal arm $i \notin \mathcal{C}^*$ and $j > L_C + 1$, we have \mathbb{E}[N_{i\sigma_{i(j)}}^{(1)}(T)] \leq \frac{\beta(1+\epsilon)^2 \log \log T}{D(p_{\sigma_{i(j)},i}||p_{\sigma_{i(L_C+1)},i})} + O(K) + O(\frac{1}{\epsilon^2}), where $\beta > 2$ and $\epsilon > 0$ are constants.
